newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa trucking strike starts despite mediation.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa trucking strike starts despite mediation.

text.p: The national trucking strike by around 36,000 workers kicked off on Wednesday morning despite a last-ditch attempt by the Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration (CCMA) to seek a resolution, a union official said.

Transport and General Workers' Union (TGWU) national organiser Thulani Dlamini told Reuters the CCMA, set up in terms of the new Labour Relations Act, had mediated between employers and unions Tuesday night but no resolution had been found.
He said the strike would start Wednesday morning at major venues throughout the country including Johannesburg, the Western Cape, Vanderbijlpark, Empangeni, Durban and Pretoria.
"Mediation has not failed...rather there was no progress on the first day and the strike is therefore going ahead," Dlamini said.
Another meeting, where the CCMA would mediate between unions and employers, was scheduled for Wednesday afternoon.
The strike could affect major sectors of the economy including banking, air freight, waste companies, livestock vehicles, and the ferrying of chemicals and fuels.
Trucker blockades on major highways are also a possibility if employers do not confiscate trucks from workers.

Employers and the seven unions organised in the sector are deadlocked over wages and working conditions, with union's last revised wage demand at 12.5 percent across-the-board from an original 14 to 18 percent across-the-board increase.
Employers, represented by the Road Freight Association, have upped their offer to 10 percent across-the-board from an original nine percent.
